1.note: Hos 12:9 is Ephraim's proud boast before his fall. אוֹן is "wealth" in Hosea and "strength" in the line before ("strength and vigor"); the quotation hints at the loss that follows.

2.note: יוֹנָה is both "Jonah" and "a dove" (a common image of moaning, Isa 38:14). The masculine בְּצֵאתוֹ "when he came out" points to the prophet.

3.he: לְחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל וְנַחֲלַת שַׁדַּי מִמְּרוֹמִים
3.note: In Job 31:2 "the portion of God from above" is a person's lot. Here the phrase names Moses, God's own portion, to whom the hosts of heaven bring peace; the next lines describe him.

4.note: This line has no rhyme partner (the lines before and after rhyme in pairs), and its sense is uncertain: perhaps a soul whose pearl-like qualities show from within (compare Ps 45:14 פְּנִימָה). A line may be missing from the source.

5.note: Uncertain. Perhaps the call to heaven and earth as witnesses (Deut 32:1) and the joining of the upper and lower worlds in the giving of the Torah.

6.note: A pun on הַיֵּצֶר "the (evil) inclination" and הַיּוֹצֵר "the Creator", two words from the same letters.

7.note: יָד is "a monument, a memorial" (1 Sam 15:12, Isa 56:5). It can also be read "gave him a hand (a share) at the head of the pillar", that is, first place. The image is uncertain.

8.note: Read as from פקד "to remember, visit" (God's remembering of the needy). The pointing מְפַקֵּד can also be a participle, "to the one who commands salvation", that is, Moses.

9.he: עֵת חָרְבוּ מֵימֵי יְשׁוּעוֹת הָ- / יִיתָ כְּמוֹ פֶלֶג בְּתוֹךְ צָיוֹן
9.note: The Hebrew splits the word הָיִיתָ "you were" across the two half-lines. צָיוֹן is pointed as "dry land" (Isa 32:2), a play on צִיּוֹן "Zion", which ends the last line of the poem.
